q: most influential architect of the 20th century
who is the most influential architect
a: Many consider Le Corbusier (Charles-Edouard Jeanneret, 1887-1965) the most influential architect of the 20th century. His five points of architecture (pilotis, roof garden, open floor plan, ribbon windows, and free facade) became fundamental principles of modernist design. Other contenders include Frank Lloyd Wright (organic architecture, Fallingwater, Guggenheim Museum), Ludwig Mies van der Rohe (less is more, Barcelona Pavilion, Seagram Building), Walter Gropius (founder of the Bauhaus school), Louis Kahn (monumental modernism, Salk Institute), and Frank Gehry (deconstructivism, Guggenheim Bilbao). Le Corbusier influence is arguably the most far-reaching because his ideas shaped urban planning, housing design, and architectural education worldwide through his writings (Towards an Architecture) and his work for the Congres Internationaux d Architecture Moderne (CIAM).
